CONSENT TO PARTICIPATE IN A RESEARCH STUDY

Title of study: A Randomized Trial of Adaptive Interferometric Screening for Early Retinal Disease
Protocol number: RVP-2026-014
Principal investigator: Dr. Ingrid Vasconcelos-Amaru, MD
Sponsor: Kestrel Ophthalmic Research Foundation
Institution: Ridgeway Valley Eye Institute, Asheville, North Carolina
IRB approval date: February 3, 2026
Version: 3.1

INVITATION

You are being asked to take part in a research study. This form explains the study so that you can decide whether to take part. Taking part is voluntary. Please read it, ask any question you have, and take as long as you need to decide.

WHY THIS STUDY IS BEING DONE

Early retinal disease is often missed by current screening. This study tests whether an adaptive interferometric device detects it earlier than the standard fundus photograph. About 480 people will take part at three sites.

WHAT WILL HAPPEN

If you agree, you will be assigned by chance, like the flip of a coin, to one of two groups. Neither you nor your doctor will choose the group. One group receives the adaptive scan in addition to the standard photograph; the other receives the standard photograph alone. You will have four visits over eighteen months. Each visit takes about ninety minutes and includes an eye examination, imaging, and a short questionnaire. At the first and last visits a blood sample of about two teaspoons will be drawn.

RISKS AND DISCOMFORTS

The imaging uses low-power light and is not known to injure the eye. The dilating drops sting briefly and blur your vision for four to six hours; you should not drive until it clears. Blood draws can cause bruising, soreness, and rarely fainting or infection. There may be risks that are not yet known. If new information becomes available that may affect your willingness to continue, we will tell you.

BENEFITS

You may not benefit from taking part. The scan may detect disease earlier in your case, but that is not certain. What is learned may help other people in the future.

ALTERNATIVES

You do not have to take part. Your alternative is to continue with the standard screening your doctor recommends. Choosing not to take part will not affect your medical care, your relationship with your doctors, or any benefit you are otherwise entitled to.

COSTS AND PAYMENT

There is no cost to you for the study visits, the imaging, or the blood draws. You will be paid $75 for each completed visit, up to $300. Your regular medical care is billed to you or your insurer as usual.

INJURY

If you are injured as a direct result of taking part, the Institution will provide or arrange for necessary medical treatment. The Sponsor has agreed to pay the reasonable cost of treating an injury caused by the study procedures that is not covered by your insurance. You do not give up any of your legal rights by signing this form.

CONFIDENTIALITY

Your study records are kept confidential to the extent permitted by law. Records are labeled with a code rather than your name, and the key is held by the principal investigator. Your records may be reviewed by the Sponsor, the Institutional Review Board, and the Food and Drug Administration. A description of this trial will be available on ClinicalTrials.gov as required by law; that site will not include information that can identify you.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION AND WITHDRAWAL

Taking part is voluntary. You may refuse to take part, and you may stop at any time, without penalty and without losing any benefit to which you are otherwise entitled. If you stop, data already collected may still be used. The investigator may end your participation if it is in your medical interest or if the study is stopped.

WHOM TO CONTACT

For a question about the study or a research-related injury, contact Dr. Ingrid Vasconcelos-Amaru at (828) 555-0164. For a question about your rights as a research participant, or to report a concern, contact the Ridgeway Valley Institutional Review Board at (828) 555-0190 or irb@ridgewayvalley.org.

CONSENT

I have read this form. My questions have been answered. I agree to take part in this study. I will be given a signed copy of this form.
